## Documentation, October 2026: sector chapters aligned with the new CIMS hierarchy

- Rewrote every sector chapter around the CIMS hierarchy in the technology database (`cims_hierarchy.csv`), with a generated process flowchart (see @sec-figure-style) and, after each process step, the technologies that compete there.
- Added sub-sector chapters for chemicals (nitrogen, chlor-alkali, and petrochemicals), non-ferrous metals (aluminum, and base metals), natural gas (methane emissions), and crude oil (oil sands).
- Merged the Ethanol and Biodiesel chapters into Biofuels, retitled Chemical Products as Chemicals and Carbon Dioxide Removal as Direct Air Capture, and grouped the sector chapters into five parts.
- Retitled Petroleum Crude as Crude Oil, Metal Smelting and Refining as Non-Ferrous Metals, and the two transportation chapters as Passenger Transportation and Freight Transportation. Page addresses and cross-reference labels keep the hierarchy's sector names.
- The flowchart script now orders the bends of flows that share a gap between columns, and the ports they use on each card, so that flows don't cross.
- Rebuilt the General Services part from the hierarchy: machine drive, industrial heat and steam (formerly low-temperature industrial heat), cogeneration and on-site power, HVAC and lighting (new), fuel blends (new), and CCUS.
- Dropped the indicative literature cost and maturity tables; each technology now shows a short description and its type from the database.
- Rewrote the sector and General Services chapters in plain language, with fuller process descriptions and citations to the technology database's sources (collected in `tech-data_references.bib` by `_technology-blocks/build_tech_data_bib.py`). Flowcharts now show each sector's structure rather than today's purchased fuels.
- Renamed all documentation files to the project's naming convention; old page addresses redirect to the new ones.
- Nodes the hierarchy added ahead of the CIMS model inputs, as listed in the technology database's `hierarchy-change-requests.md`, are documented as part of the structure: the iron and steel coke, hot-metal, and direct-reduced-iron services; direct air capture; mining on-site power; crude transmission, pumping, produced water, and oil sands tailings; pulp and paper effluent treatment; ceramics, gypsum, and the cement binder nodes; nitric acid, urea, and fertilizer; non-ferrous metals CCS, the acid plant, and alumina calcination; synthetic fuels; and coal-mine methane.
